lines.text: If you stepped out of a spaceship onto the surface of Venus, how long could your body survive?
The terrifying answer is less than one single second.
Venus is trapped under a runaway greenhouse effect of ninety-six percent carbon dioxide.
Surface temperatures reach a blistering nine hundred degrees Fahrenheit, hot enough to melt solid lead.
The atmospheric pressure is ninety times heavier than Earth's, equivalent to being three thousand feet underwater.
Your skull and ribcage would be crushed flat like an aluminum soda can instantly.
Thick clouds above rain corrosive sulfuric acid that evaporates before touching the scorched basalt ground.
Venus is the absolute closest thing to a literal hell in our solar system.
